page: Microsoft Azure F1ads_v7 is a single-core virtual machine belonging to the Fadsv7 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 1 vCPU, 1 physical core, and 1 thread per core, paired with 4.0 GB of system memory. For local storage, the instance is equipped with a 118 GB local disk and supports Premium Storage. It runs under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data highlights a strong contrast between single-threaded and multi-threaded or memory-intensive operations. The dedicated AMD EPYC processor delivers top-tier single-core CPU performance, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 3541.88 and high single-threaded compression speeds, with gzip compression reaching 38.66 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 16.95 GB/sec. However, due to its single-core limitation, multi-core performance is weak, matching the single-core score. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only small block bandwidth at 205.2 GB/sec and large block read-only bandwidth at 39.12 GB/sec, both falling into the bottom 25%. Large block write bandwidth is average at 31.44 GB/sec.

Given its hardware profile, the F1ads_v7 is suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads that benefit from high CPU clock speeds but do not require extensive parallel processing or massive memory allocations. Examples include basic single-threaded utility scripts, lightweight background tasks, or simple text processing. It is less suitable for database operations, high-throughput web serving, or multi-threaded applications, as reflected in its weak Passmark database score of 1293.5 and poor static web serving throughput of 2.63 GB/sec. The instance offers a cost-efficient entry point for dedicated CPU resources without the overhead of multi-core configurations.
